column4: [EN-01] Hive telemetry simulator v1 with stylized-fact tests
column5:
h3. User story
As the ML and backend teams, we need realistic simulated hive telemetry with labeled events so that we can build and test models and the dashboard without client data.

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Given a scenario YAML and a seed, when the simulator runs, then it writes telemetry, events, colony ground truth, weather and a manifest, identical on every run
# Given the default scenario, when the stylized-fact tests run, then brood temperature, daily weight cycle, rain, swarm, absconding and humidity facts all pass
# Given the observed columns, when compared with the DHT11 datasheet, then values are integers within its range and carry quality flags
# Given six scenarios (baseline, swarm season, abscond/collapse, sensor faults, quiet hive, battery node), when generated with seed 42, then all finish in under a minute

column4: [US09] Automated Varroa mite detection
column5:
h3. User story
As a beekeeper, I want the system to automatically identify Varroa mites on returning bees so that I can start treatment before the infestation spreads.

h3. Acceptance criteria
# Given a sharp bee crop at >= 8 px/mm, when stage 2 runs, then it outputs p(varroa) and the frame record carries it
# Given synthetic validation crops (held-out sprites), when evaluated, then recall and precision for varroa are reported (tier S)
# Given the public Varroa datasets, when available, then recall >= 0.75 and precision >= 0.70 on their test split (tier P target)
# Given a rolling window, when bees are classified, then the Varroa index is reported with its count and 95 % Wilson interval

column4: [US10] Small hive beetle and Asian hornet detection
column5:
h3. User story
As a beekeeper, I want the system to detect small hive beetles and Asian hornets at the entrance so that I can intervene before they damage the colony.

h3. Acceptance criteria

As the team, we need an enclosure that keeps the node dry, cool enough and away from propolis so that it survives outdoors (NFR-03, NFR-04, NFR-07).
